Series::tensor¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

torch::Tensor Series::tensor() const

Availability. This method exists only when the library is built with -DPLUSS_ENABLE_TORCH=ON. In a build without LibTorch the method is not compiled and <torch/torch.h> is not required.

What It Does¶

Exposes the series to LibTorch as a torch::Tensor view — no data is copied. The returned tensor shares storage with the series: it sees the same bytes, keeps that storage alive for as long as it is referenced, and reflects writes made through either handle.

It is the reverse of pluss::series::from_torch. There is no free to_torch function — construction from a tensor is a factory call, and the trip back is this method.

The view carries the series’ dtype, shape, and strides, so a non-contiguous or offset series exports as a strided tensor rather than being made contiguous first. If a downstream call needs contiguous input, call .contiguous() on the torch::Tensor (or on the Series beforehand).

Only CPU series are supported. The dtype mapping is the natural one (Float64 <-> kFloat64, Int64 <-> kInt64, Complex64 <-> kComplexFloat, and so on).

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

torch::Tensor A CPU tensor viewing the series’ storage, with matching dtype, shape, and strides.

Raises if the series is undefined, if its dtype has no torch equivalent, or if its layout is overlapping (call .contiguous() first).

Gradient¶

tensor() is a storage bridge, not a differentiable op. The returned torch::Tensor is a fresh LibTorch leaf with requires_grad == false; pluss sensitivities do not flow across the boundary in either direction.

That does not prevent training. Training data normally does not require a gradient: model parameters receive gradients when the exported tensor is used as an input. If the series’ values are themselves the parameters to optimize, enable gradients on the returned floating-point or complex tensor with requires_grad_(true).

Handing A Series To A Training Pipeline¶

The zero-copy CPU view is already a usable LibTorch tensor. This is the direct handoff when the model runs on the CPU:

auto features = prepared_features.tensor();
auto targets = prepared_targets.tensor();

optimizer.zero_grad();
auto prediction = model->forward(features);
auto loss = torch::mse_loss(prediction, targets);
loss.backward();
optimizer.step();

Neither features nor targets needs requires_grad. Backward computes gradients for the model’s registered parameters.

For accelerator training, cross the storage boundary explicitly:

torch::Device device(torch::kCUDA);
model->to(device);

auto features = prepared_features.tensor().to(device);
auto targets = prepared_targets.tensor().to(device);

optimizer.zero_grad();
auto prediction = model->forward(features);
auto loss = torch::mse_loss(prediction, targets);
loss.backward();
optimizer.step();

tensor() itself is CPU-only and zero-copy. The subsequent .to(device) is a LibTorch transfer that allocates device-owned storage. The device tensor no longer depends on the series’ buffer and can outlive every pluss handle.

If the values, rather than a model, are what you intend to optimize, make that choice explicit:

auto parameter = initial_values.tensor().to(device).detach();
parameter.requires_grad_(true);

auto loss = parameter.square().sum();
loss.backward();
std::cout << parameter.grad() << "\n";

The call to detach() documents that this is the beginning of a new training graph. On the CPU, omitting .to(device) preserves aliasing with the series; optimizer writes will then change the shared buffer. Use .clone() first when training should not mutate data still owned conceptually by pluss.

Examples¶

These examples require a -DPLUSS_ENABLE_TORCH=ON build.

Example 1. Export a series as a tensor view.

auto a = pluss::make_series({{1.0, 2.0}, {3.0, 4.0}});
torch::Tensor t = a.tensor();
std::cout << t << "\n";

Output¶

 1  2
 3  4
[ CPUDoubleType{2,2} ]

Example 2. The view is live: a write through the tensor is visible in the series.

auto a = pluss::make_series({{1.0, 2.0}, {3.0, 4.0}});
torch::Tensor t = a.tensor();
t[0][1] = 42.0;

pluss::series::print(std::cout, a);

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 1.0000 42.0000 ⎤
⎣ 3.0000  4.0000 ⎦

Example 3. An offset view (here a row slice) exports its real data, not the whole backing buffer.

auto big = pluss::series::arange(0, 12).reshape({3, 4});
torch::Tensor rows = big.slice(0, 1, 3).tensor();
std::cout << rows << "\n";

Output¶

  4   5   6   7
  8   9  10  11
[ CPULongType{2,4} ]

Example 4. A round trip aliases the same buffer.

torch::Tensor x = torch::ones({4}, torch::kFloat32);
torch::Tensor y = pluss::series::from_torch(x).tensor();
std::cout << "same data_ptr: " << (x.data_ptr() == y.data_ptr() ? "yes" : "no") << "\n";

Output¶

same data_ptr: yes

Example 5. An undefined series raises.

try {
  pluss::Series u;
  (void)u.tensor();
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

to_torch: undefined

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The tensor is a view. If a later pluss operation replaces the series’ storage (many in-place ops allocate fresh storage rather than mutating), a tensor captured earlier keeps pointing at the old buffer. Re-export after such an operation.

  • No autodiff crosses the boundary. A torch::Tensor from tensor() does not carry pluss sensitivities, and requires_grad on the torch side does not reach back.

  • Direct export is CPU-only. Transfer the returned tensor with .to(device) for accelerator training; that transfer intentionally creates new storage.

  • Overlapping layouts (e.g. a stride-0 broadcast) are rejected; materialize with .contiguous() first.

  • The method is absent entirely in a non-torch build — guard call sites with #ifdef PLUSS_ENABLE_TORCH if your code must compile both ways.

Summary¶

tensor() bridges a series into LibTorch:

  • zero-copy torch::Tensor view sharing storage, dtype, shape, and strides

  • immediately usable as CPU training input, or transferable to an accelerator

  • requires a -DPLUSS_ENABLE_TORCH=ON build

  • the reverse of pluss::series::from_torch; there is no free to_torch

  • not an autodiff boundary — grad is managed separately on each side

See Also¶

  • pluss::series::from_torch: the other direction — build a series from a torch::Tensor.

  • Series::contiguous: force a dense layout before export if a consumer needs one.

  • Series::to: change dtype before crossing the boundary.
